newsitem.title: USA: IPO SPOTLIGHT - Gargoyles IPO should shine.
newsitem.headline: IPO SPOTLIGHT - Gargoyles IPO should shine.

text.p: Sunglass-maker Gargoyles Inc is expected to have a shining initial public offering today, boosted by a hot niche industry and interest by institutional investors.
The offering of 2,857,145 shares of Gargoyles Inc common stock priced at $16, above its estimated range of $13 to $15, and is expected to begin trading today, Smith Barney said.
Vince Slavin, who tracks IPOs for Cantor Fitzgerald, told Reuters "vibes from the Street" are that it will be a hot issue.

"There will be institutional interest followed by strong manufacturing and retail interest," said Cantor Fitzgerald IPO analyst Vince Slavin. "With Smith Barney strong in the retail industry, they could make this deal work."
"(The performance sunglasses industry) is a very hot ... Look at the stock performance of Oakley (Inc )," said Linda Killian from Renaissance Capital Corp, a firm that anaylzes IPOs.
"Gargoyles is a little bit more of a niche player," taking high performance athletic sunglasses and moving them into the mainstream, she said.
Oakley Inc, an Irvine, Calif.-based sunglasses company went public at $23 in August. Its shares have almost doubled, now trading around $42.
"Gargoyles probably won't be that hot (long-term) but it will be very explosive coming out of the starting gate," said John Fitzgibbon, editor of the IPO Aftermarket.

Gargoyles posted a net loss of $2.6 million for the six months ended June 30, 1996 on sales of $17.6 million, compared with a net profit of $128,000 for the same period last year on sales of $9.1 million.
